# 出曜經

**ID:** T0212
**Volume:** T04
**Category:** 本緣部類
**Original Category:** 本緣部
**Byline:** 姚秦 竺佛念譯
**Dynasty:** 前秦
**Date:** 374–383
**Juans:** 30
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T0212

## Contributors
- 竺佛念 (A000435)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A thirty-fascicle Latter-Qín 姚秦 translation of the *Udānavarga* — [法救](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E6%95%91) Dharmatrāta's compilation of Buddhist gnomic-verse — together with extensive prose *avadāna*-commentary pairing each verse with a narrative occasion. Translated by [竺佛念](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E4%BD%9B%E5%BF%B5) Zhú Fóniàn (= Buddhanandi). This is the most extensive Chinese *Udānavarga* / *Dharmapada*-with-commentary text. The work opens with a translator's preface (《出曜經》序) attributing the underlying compilation to Dharmatrāta 法救 (referred to as "Vasumitra's maternal uncle"): 「《出曜經》者，婆須密舅法救菩薩之所撰也，集…」 ("The *Chūyào jīng* is what the Bodhisattva Dharmatrāta — [Vasumitra](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A9%86%E9%A0%88%E5%AF%86)-the-elder's maternal uncle — compiled, collecting…").

**Abstract**

T212 is the most-extensive of the Chinese *Udānavarga* texts: a verse-by-verse Chinese rendering with extensive prose-narrative commentary, of which both verse and commentary are translated together. The work is the principal pre-Tang Chinese witness for the Sarvāstivādin *Udānavarga* tradition, with the prose-commentary providing extensive *avadāna*-narrative occasions for each verse. The translation can be dated to Zhú Fóniàn's documented Latter-Qín activity, c. 398–399 CE under Yáo Xìng's patronage at Cháng'ān; the *Chū sānzàng jì jí* preserves the relevant chronological details.

T212 is foundational for East-Asian Buddhist gnomic-verse literature; together with [T210](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0067) (the shorter Wú-period *Dharmapada*) and [T213](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0070) (Tiānxīzāi's late-tenth-century *Udānavarga*), it constitutes the principal Chinese-canon set of *Dharmapada* / *Udānavarga* witnesses.
